title: Trump Signals F-35 Return and Sanctions Relief for Turkey; Syria and Israel Hold Jordan Talks on De-Escalation
subhead: Washington dangles a reset in defense ties just as Ankara's confrontation with Israel over Syria enters a new diplomatic phase, with Damascus and Jerusalem meeting in Amman with Turkey at the center of the agenda.

sections.heading: US-Turkey: Trump Opens Door to F-35 Return and Sanctions Relief
sections.body: President Donald Trump said he will consider giving Turkey F-35 fighter jets and added that the United States will lift sanctions on Ankara, according to ABC News. The remarks mark the most concrete signal yet of a US-Turkey defense reset after years of friction over Ankara's Russian S-400 purchase, which triggered Turkey's removal from the F-35 program and CAATSA sanctions in 2019-2020. The statement comes amid a broader regional realignment in which Washington has courted Ankara on Iran and Syria policy.
sections.whyItMatters: If realized, this would reverse a decade of US defense estrangement with a key NATO ally and reshape Turkey's procurement calculus — though the S-400 question and congressional resistance remain unresolved hurdles.

sections.heading: Syria-Israel: Jordan Talks Put Turkey at the Center of De-Escalation
sections.body: Syria and Israel held talks in Jordan addressing de-escalation and Israel-Turkey tensions, the South China Morning Post and Türkiye Today report. The meeting follows Israeli strikes on Syrian territory and comes as Ankara deepens its military partnership with Damascus. Turkey's Defense Ministry has said it will press ahead with its military partnership with Damascus and continue helping Syria rebuild its armed forces, defying Israeli warnings, per endtimeheadlines.org. Israel Hayom frames the dynamic as Turkey cementing its military and economic grip over Syria.
sections.whyItMatters: Direct Syria-Israel contact with Turkey as the unspoken third party signals that the Israel-Turkey rivalry over Syria is being managed through channels rather than left to escalate — but the underlying competition over Syria's reconstruction and security is unresolved.

sections.heading: Israel-Turkey Rivalry: Netanyahu-Erdogan Spat Continues
sections.body: Le Monde reports the Israel-Turkey tensions expose a personal and strategic rivalry between Netanyahu and Erdogan, after the Israeli premier called Erdogan an 'antisemitic dictator' on August 21. Daily Sabah argues Netanyahu is clinging to an anti-Türkiye campaign amid Likud's decline, while Ynet and Haaretz both published analyses of how the once-close alliance collapsed. CGTN ties the deepening tensions to both the Syria file and Ankara's Interpol red notice request for Netanyahu over the Gaza flotilla.
sections.whyItMatters: The feud is now as much about domestic politics on both sides as about Syria — Netanyahu's electoral position and Erdogan's regional posture are feeding a cycle of escalation that neither appears willing to break.

sections.heading: E1 Settlement: Turkey Joins Regional Condemnation
sections.body: Turkey was among eight nations that jointly condemned Israel's E1 settlement plan, demanding international sanctions and an immediate halt, according to Kurdistan24 and The Jerusalem Post. Jordan, the UAE and other countries joined the statement, with The Arab Weekly reporting Arab and Muslim foreign ministers condemned the Israeli West Bank settlement plans. Jordan News framed the E1 plan as a test of whether condemnation can become real pressure on Israel.
sections.whyItMatters: Ankara is aligning with the Arab consensus against Israeli settlement expansion, reinforcing its pro-Palestinian posture at a moment when it is simultaneously confronting Israel over Syria — a two-front diplomatic squeeze on Jerusalem.

sections.heading: Economy: Central Bank Ends Physical Gold Conversion Scheme
sections.body: Turkey's central bank has officially repealed the regulation that brought under-the-mattress gold into the financial system, Hürriyet Daily News reports. The scheme, which allowed households to convert physical gold into lira-backed accounts, is being wound down. Separately, foreign arrivals improved in July, narrowing the annual decline, per CryptoRank — a tentative sign of tourism recovery. The moves come as Ankara finalizes its Medium-Term Program, with JPMorgan seeing room for the CBRT to start cutting rates in September.
sections.whyItMatters: Ending the gold conversion scheme signals the central bank is confident enough in lira stability to phase out a crisis-era tool, while improving tourism data offers a rare bright spot for the current account.

sections.heading: Kurdish File: Progress in North Syria Buffer Zone, SDF-KDP Rapprochement
sections.body: The US-led coalition reported 'good progress' in the north Syria buffer zone, according to Kurdpress, while the Syrian KDP welcomed an SDF offer for joining forces and Syrian Kurds are seeking US mediation for stability in northeast Syria. These developments touch directly on Turkey's security concerns along its southern border, where Ankara has long sought to prevent a unified Kurdish autonomous zone.
sections.whyItMatters: A KDP-SDF rapprochement and coalition progress in the buffer zone could either ease or complicate Turkey's calculus — Ankara watches any consolidation of Kurdish forces in northeast Syria warily, even as it deepens ties with Damascus.

sections.heading: Energy: Eastern Mediterranean Contest Sharpens
sections.body: El País reports a new energy war in the Eastern Mediterranean in which Egypt and Turkey stand to gain, while Cyprus has protested to the UN over Turkey's planned undersea gas pipeline, per The National Herald. Modern Diplomacy separately flags that Cyprus could become the next military flashpoint in the Turkey-Israel tensions. The moves build on Ankara's 'Four Seas' energy vision announced with Damascus last week.
sections.whyItMatters: Turkey is positioning itself as a hub for Eastern Mediterranean gas at the same time its maritime disputes with Cyprus and Greece remain live — energy ambition and military tension are converging in the same waters.

bottomLine: Today's picture is defined by two parallel tracks: Washington signaling a possible F-35 and sanctions reset with Ankara, and a new diplomatic channel opening between Syria and Israel in Jordan with Turkey as the central concern. The US overture, if it holds, would be the most significant shift in Turkey's defense relationship with the West in years. Meanwhile, the Israel-Turkey rivalry over Syria is being channeled into talks rather than left to escalate, though the E1 settlement row and Eastern Mediterranean energy contest keep multiple pressure points alive. The central bank's decision to end its gold conversion scheme and improving tourism data suggest the economy is stabilizing as Ankara finalizes its Medium-Term Program.
